title: I Let the Cheese-Cave Shelf Clock Catch the Member Who Took My Numbered Wheels

parts.text: I stepped into shelf D at 9:05 a.m. and member Helene was already using my numbered wheels. The board said: ONE SHELF. NINETY DAYS. WHEELS STAY LABELED. I was thirty-eight, cave steward, holding a clipboard that listed our affine. Helene shrugged. "Members share the cave." I photographed the board, the booking, and her rind on my shelf. Then I asked for the shelf clock. At 9:13 the dairy desk pinged why Helene's rind sat on shelf D. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The dairy desk can see Helene's rind on shelf D during our affine.

social.video_title: She took my numbered wheels off shelf D — Part 1/2
social.description: Cheese cave, a member on my shelf, a ninety-day clock she posted. I logged the rind. Would you have asked for the shelf clock?

parts.text: Helene called it turning until the desk asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the shelf still. The wheels went back to my numbered paper. Helene ran a slot of their own and told the next member atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: MEMBERS DO NOT SHARE A LABELED SHELF. I keep our affine on a labeled tag. Helene brown-bags her rinds. The cave finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Members do not share a labeled shelf — Part 2/2
social.description: Shelf clock, numbered wheels, and a second line on the board. Was turning ever our affine?
